attributes.residual: EXACTLY 2 BYTES, and they are the whole remaining flip blocker for this TU. Our pool has 0.5f at +0x38 and 2.0f at +0x3c; the target has 2.0f at +0x38 and 0.5f at +0x3c. datadiff --sections: .sdata2 size 0x70 (EQUAL, was a 0x78-vs-0x0 SIZE MISMATCH), 98.2% bytes equal - 110 of 112 bytes, the two differing bytes being the leading byte of each transposed float. MECHANISM, fully named and measured: MWCC lays .sdata2 out strictly in literal CREATION order, and creation order is the textual order of literals within each code-generated function, functions taken in definition order. Both entries are created inside pbProjCalc (our labels @116=0.5f, @117=2.0f, consecutive). The target therefore parses a 2.0f BEFORE the first 0.5f at the vpcx line - yet the target's TEXT uses 0.5f first (at +0x364) and 2.0f only at +0x3e8, and its emission order matches our current UNMOVED source. So the target source contains a 2.0f occurrence that is textually earlier than the centers but whose code is NOT emitted early. WHAT IS RULED OUT: the ratio-block move (A), the inline device (B), the division form (C); a hole-filling pool allocator (disproved arithmetically - our pre-fix pool would have packed to 0x70 with zero padding under hole-filling, but MWCC actually emitted 0x78 with pads, so layout is strictly creation order); and creation by any function other than pbProjCalc (the entries sit between debugScissor's 2^52 magic and pbProjCalc's 0.008726646261111111, which brackets them into pbProjCalc). WHAT REMAINS UNTRIED, and is the next agent's most likely lever: a SECOND code-generated-then-dead-stripped static sitting between debugScissor and pbProjCalc, symmetric with the pbWindowDefaults device this pass proved; or a genuine early 2.0f expression inside pbProjCalc lines 364-422 that we have currently reconstructed in a 2.0f-free form (the w2/h2 half-dimension reads at lines 407-408 are the most suspicious candidates). Do NOT reach for webfrank: this is a DATA-section residual and webfrank is a text postprocessor.
